section.sectionSummaryBrief: One might think that since nature operates uniformly, it obscures G-d's involvement, and only miracles reveal Him, but the maamar explains that through avodah, the revelation of the supernatural is drawn into nature itself.
section.t: And seemingly, it could be said,
that since the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, conducts the world according to nature is always uniform
[for each and every day the sun rises in the east and sets in the west,
and likewise in all matters of nature],
therefore it is not openly apparent that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the One who conducts the world, and there is room for error that the world conducts itself on its own9,
and through the miracles that sometimes the Holy One, blessed be He, changes the conduct of nature,
this proves that also the conduct of nature10
is from the Holy One, blessed be He.
But according to this,
the perfection of nature is that it should be openly apparent that nature is Elokus,
and in the maamar it says that through the avodah
(of mesiras nefesh)
the revelation of that which is above nature is drawn into nature.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The root of nature is from the Name Elokim, and the root of miracles is from the Name Havayah, corresponding to lower knowledge and upper knowledge respectively.
section.t: And it is explained in several discourses11
that the root of nature is from the Name Elokim
(Elokim has the numerical value of haTeva12),
and the root of miracles is from the Name Havayah.
And it explains there,
that in the Name Havayah is upper knowledge,
that above there is yesh and below there is ayin,
meaning that all of existence is nothing and naught and is considered as nothing before Him,
and in the Name Elokim is lower knowledge,
that creation is from ayin to yesh,
meaning that the creations are an existence of yesh
[and the Elokis power that brings them into existence is called by the name ayin,
an ayin that is not grasped].
[And it could be said,
that it is similar to what is explained elsewhere13
that the coming into being from the Name Elokim is in a manner of enclothement
(Bereishis bara Elokim14),
for this indicates that it is a source for the matter of coming into being.
Therefore the creations that come into being from it occupy place relative to it,
and their bittul is only bittul hayesh – lower knowledge that below there is yesh.
And the coming into being from the Name Havayah is in a manner of automatically
(Yehallelu et shem Havayah ki hu tzivah venivrau15),
for this indicates that it is wondrous relative to the matter of coming into being,
therefore the creations that come into being from it do not occupy place relative to it,
bittul bimetzius – upper knowledge that below there is ayin].

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as the Names Havayah and Elokim correspond to upper and lower knowledge, so too miracles and nature correspond to these levels, and through miracles drawn into the world, the unification of lower and upper knowledge is achieved.
section.t: And it is explained in the discourses11,
that just as it is regarding the Names,
that in the Name Havayah is upper knowledge and in the Name Elokim is lower knowledge,
so too is it regarding the matter of miracle and nature
(which are drawn from Havayah and Elokim),
that the conduct of nature is from the aspect of lower knowledge,
and the miracles that are above nature are from the aspect of upper knowledge.
[And it could be said,
that the connection of miracle and nature to upper knowledge and lower knowledge is not only from the perspective of their root,
that the root of miracles is from Havayah and the root of nature is from Elokim,
but also from the perspective of the matter of miracle and nature themselves.
And the explanation is,
that the conduct of nature is that the Holy One, blessed be He, conducts each creation according to its own nature,
for this indicates that in this conduct,
the creations occupy place,
below there is yesh.
And miraculous conduct is that the Holy One, blessed be He, conducts the world according to His will and not according to the characteristic and nature of the creations,
for in this conduct,
the creations do not occupy place,
below there is ayin].
And through the miracles that are drawn into the world,
that also into nature the revelation of that which is above nature is drawn,
the unification of lower knowledge and upper knowledge is made,
to be one in one16,
that also in lower knowledge the revelation of upper knowledge shines.
